title: CTS Christian Education — Unit 2: You — The Teacher

blocks.en: Christian Education — Unit 2: You — The Teacher
blocks.es_reference: Educación Cristiana — Unidad 2: Usted — El Maestro

blocks.en: From this unit forward the teaching voice is Andi's, drawn from her contribution to WiseSpeak (1993). The framing is light; the pedagogy is hers.
blocks.es_reference: A partir de esta unidad la voz docente es la de Andi, extraída de su contribución a WiseSpeak (1993). El marco es ligero; la pedagogía es suya.

blocks.en: Unit 2 · 2 Timothy 2:2 · The Teacher
blocks.es_reference: Unidad 2 · 2 Timoteo 2:2 · El Maestro

blocks.en: You — The Teacher
blocks.es_reference: Usted — El Maestro

blocks.en: "Commit these to faithful men who will be able to teach others also."
blocks.es_reference: «Encarga a hombres fieles que sean idóneos para enseñar también a otros».

blocks.en: Unit Scripture: "And the things that you have heard from me among many witnesses, commit these to faithful men who will be able to teach others also." — 2 Timothy 2:2 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: Escritura de la Unidad: «Y lo que has oído de mí ante muchos testigos, esto encarga a hombres fieles que sean idóneos para enseñar también a otros». — 2 Timoteo 2:2 (RVG)

blocks.en: Orientation: The Teacher Is the Most Important Element
blocks.es_reference: Orientación: El maestro es el elemento más importante

blocks.en: The teacher is the most important element in the teaching-learning process.
blocks.es_reference: El maestro es el elemento más importante en el proceso de enseñanza-aprendizaje.

blocks.en: That sentence is the thesis of this whole course. It is more important than the curriculum. It is more important than the room. It is more important than the textbook. It is more important than the lesson plan. The student will remember the teacher long after the lesson is forgotten. The student will be shaped by the teacher's character long after the words of the lesson have faded from memory.
blocks.es_reference: Esa oración es la tesis de todo este curso. Es más importante que el currículo. Es más importante que el salón. Es más importante que el libro de texto. Es más importante que el plan de lección. El estudiante recordará al maestro mucho después de que la lección sea olvidada. El estudiante será moldeado por el carácter del maestro mucho después de que las palabras de la lección hayan desaparecido de la memoria.

blocks.en: Paul wrote to Timothy, "And the things that you have heard from me among many witnesses, commit these to faithful men who will be able to teach others also" (2 Timothy 2:2). Notice how Paul describes the teacher. The teacher is a faithful man. The teacher is one who has heard the things of God among witnesses. The teacher is able to teach others. The teacher receives what he has heard and passes it on. There is no curriculum mentioned. There is no classroom. There is no textbook. There is just a faithful person who can hand the truth on to another faithful person who will hand it on again.
blocks.es_reference: Pablo escribió a Timoteo: «Y lo que has oído de mí ante muchos testigos, esto encarga a hombres fieles que sean idóneos para enseñar también a otros» (2 Timoteo 2:2). Note cómo Pablo describe al maestro. El maestro es un hombre fiel. El maestro es uno que ha oído las cosas de Dios entre testigos. El maestro es idóneo para enseñar a otros. El maestro recibe lo que ha oído y lo pasa adelante. No se menciona un currículo. No se menciona un aula. No se menciona un libro de texto. Sólo se menciona una persona fiel que puede entregar la verdad a otra persona fiel que la entregará otra vez.

blocks.en: This unit answers the question, "What kind of person should that teacher be?" Six things stand out from the New Testament's description of those Paul, Peter, and James trained for the teaching ministry.
blocks.es_reference: Esta unidad responde a la pregunta: «¿Qué clase de persona debe ser ese maestro?» Seis cosas se destacan de la descripción que el Nuevo Testamento da de los que Pablo, Pedro y Santiago entrenaron para el ministerio de enseñanza.

blocks.en: Person of God · Student of the Word · Servant · Student of the Students · Student of the Teaching Process · Person of Prayer
blocks.es_reference: Persona de Dios · Estudiante de la Palabra · Siervo · Estudiante de los estudiantes · Estudiante del proceso · Persona de oración

blocks.en: The next six sections take each one in turn.
blocks.es_reference: Las siguientes seis secciones toman cada una en su turno.

blocks.en: I. A Person of God
blocks.es_reference: I. Una persona de Dios

blocks.en: The teacher must be a person of God before the teacher is anything else. A person who does not walk with God cannot lead a student to God. A person who does not know God cannot teach the student about God. A person who has not been changed by the gospel cannot expect the student to be changed by the gospel.
blocks.es_reference: El maestro debe ser una persona de Dios antes de ser cualquier otra cosa. Una persona que no anda con Dios no puede llevar a un estudiante a Dios. Una persona que no conoce a Dios no puede enseñar al estudiante acerca de Dios. Una persona que no ha sido cambiada por el evangelio no puede esperar que el estudiante sea cambiado por el evangelio.

blocks.en: This is not optional. The teacher who tries to teach what he has not himself received will run dry within a few weeks. The teacher who teaches out of an empty cup gives the students an empty drink. We cannot give what we do not have.
blocks.es_reference: Esto no es opcional. El maestro que trata de enseñar lo que él mismo no ha recibido se secará en unas pocas semanas. El maestro que enseña de una taza vacía les da a los estudiantes una bebida vacía. No podemos dar lo que no tenemos.

blocks.en: The teacher's first work, therefore, is not preparation for the lesson. The teacher's first work is preparation of the soul. Before the lesson plan is written, the teacher must be in the Word for himself. Before the questions are framed, the teacher must have answered them in his own heart. The classroom does not begin on Sunday morning. It begins on Tuesday afternoon when the teacher opens the Bible alone and asks the Holy Spirit to teach him first.
blocks.es_reference: La primera obra del maestro, por lo tanto, no es la preparación para la lección. La primera obra del maestro es la preparación del alma. Antes de que se escriba el plan de lección, el maestro debe estar en la Palabra por sí mismo. Antes de que se formulen las preguntas, el maestro debe haberlas respondido en su propio corazón. El aula no comienza el domingo por la mañana. Comienza el martes por la tarde cuando el maestro abre la Biblia a solas y le pide al Espíritu Santo que le enseñe a él primero.

blocks.en: II. A Student of the Word
blocks.es_reference: II. Un estudiante de la Palabra

blocks.en: The Word must be the teacher's constant companion. Not a reference book pulled from the shelf on Saturday night. Not a tool used only when there is a question to answer. The Word is the teacher's daily food.
blocks.es_reference: La Palabra debe ser la compañera constante del maestro. No un libro de referencia sacado del estante el sábado por la noche. No una herramienta usada sólo cuando hay una pregunta que responder. La Palabra es el alimento diario del maestro.

blocks.en: The teacher must know the Bible — what it says, what it means, how it fits together, where one passage answers another, where the Old Testament prepares for the New, where the four Gospels speak as one voice. The teacher who does not know the Bible cannot teach the Bible. The teacher will be reduced to teaching opinions about the Bible, which is something else entirely.
blocks.es_reference: El maestro debe conocer la Biblia — lo que dice, lo que significa, cómo encaja, dónde un pasaje responde a otro, dónde el Antiguo Testamento prepara el Nuevo, dónde los cuatro Evangelios hablan como una sola voz. El maestro que no conoce la Biblia no puede enseñar la Biblia. El maestro se verá reducido a enseñar opiniones sobre la Biblia, lo cual es algo enteramente diferente.

blocks.en: The teacher must also know how to use the Bible — how to find a passage, how to read it in context, how to compare Scripture with Scripture, how to apply an ancient text to a present-day question. Knowledge of the contents and skill in handling the contents are different things. The teacher needs both. A person who has read the Bible cover to cover but cannot answer a child's question on Tuesday afternoon has knowledge without skill. A person who can find any passage in seconds but does not understand what it means has skill without knowledge. The Christian Education teacher pursues both, all his life.
blocks.es_reference: El maestro también debe saber cómo usar la Biblia — cómo encontrar un pasaje, cómo leerlo en contexto, cómo comparar Escritura con Escritura, cómo aplicar un texto antiguo a una pregunta del día de hoy. El conocimiento del contenido y la habilidad para manejar el contenido son cosas diferentes. El maestro necesita ambas. Una persona que ha leído la Biblia de tapa a tapa pero no puede responder a la pregunta de un niño un martes por la tarde tiene conocimiento sin habilidad. Una persona que puede encontrar cualquier pasaje en segundos pero no comprende lo que significa tiene habilidad sin conocimiento. El maestro de Educación Cristiana busca ambos, toda su vida.

blocks.en: III. A Servant
blocks.es_reference: III. Un siervo

blocks.en: The teacher must be willing to be a servant. The teacher gives of himself in service to his students. He puts the student first. He carries the heavier weight so the student can learn.
blocks.es_reference: El maestro debe estar dispuesto a ser un siervo. El maestro se da a sí mismo en servicio a sus estudiantes. Pone al estudiante primero. Carga el peso más pesado para que el estudiante pueda aprender.

blocks.en: In our culture, the teacher is often regarded as a person of authority who stands above the student. In the New Testament the teacher is a person of authority who serves the student. Jesus gave the model: "Whosoever will be great among you, let him be your minister; and whosoever will be chief among you, let him be your servant" (Matthew 20:26–27). The teacher in the Christian Education classroom does not lord over students. The teacher kneels with them. The teacher walks them through difficult passages with patience. The teacher gives the time the lesson requires, even when the time is inconvenient. The teacher answers the small questions as carefully as the large ones, because to the small student a small question is a large question.
blocks.es_reference: En nuestra cultura, el maestro es a menudo considerado una persona de autoridad que se encuentra por encima del estudiante. En el Nuevo Testamento el maestro es una persona de autoridad que sirve al estudiante. Jesús dio el modelo: «El que entre vosotros quiera hacerse grande, será vuestro servidor; y el que entre vosotros quiera ser el primero, será vuestro siervo» (Mateo 20:26–27). El maestro en el aula de Educación Cristiana no enseñorea sobre los estudiantes. El maestro se arrodilla con ellos. Los lleva a través de pasajes difíciles con paciencia. Da el tiempo que la lección requiere, aun cuando el tiempo es inconveniente. Responde las preguntas pequeñas tan cuidadosamente como las grandes, porque para el estudiante pequeño una pregunta pequeña es una pregunta grande.

blocks.en: A teacher who serves can teach a student anything. A teacher who lords over students can teach them only resistance.
blocks.es_reference: Un maestro que sirve puede enseñar al estudiante cualquier cosa. Un maestro que enseñorea sobre los estudiantes sólo puede enseñarles resistencia.

blocks.en: IV. A Student of the Students
blocks.es_reference: IV. Un estudiante de los estudiantes

blocks.en: The teacher must be a student of the students. He must know his students — their names, their families, their needs, their interests, their backgrounds, the questions they bring with them and the questions they cannot quite ask.
blocks.es_reference: El maestro debe ser un estudiante de los estudiantes. Debe conocer a sus estudiantes — sus nombres, sus familias, sus necesidades, sus intereses, sus antecedentes, las preguntas que traen consigo y las preguntas que no pueden formular del todo.

blocks.en: Paul shows us how this is done. When Paul wrote to Timothy, he could say, "the genuine faith that is in you, which dwelt first in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice, and I am persuaded is in you also" (2 Timothy 1:5). Paul knew Timothy's grandmother. He knew Timothy's mother. He knew the household Timothy came from and the faith he had been raised in. He had taken the time to learn it. The single phrase "your grandmother Lois" tells us more about Paul's teaching ministry than a hundred sermons could. Paul taught one young man so well because Paul had first studied that one young man.
blocks.es_reference: Pablo nos muestra cómo se hace. Cuando Pablo escribió a Timoteo, podía decir: «Trayendo a la memoria la fe no fingida que hay en ti, la cual habitó primero en tu abuela Loida, y en tu madre Eunice; y estoy seguro que en ti también» (2 Timoteo 1:5). Pablo conocía a la abuela de Timoteo. Conocía a la madre de Timoteo. Conocía el hogar del cual Timoteo venía y la fe en la cual había sido criado. Había tomado el tiempo para aprenderlo. La sola frase «tu abuela Loida» nos dice más acerca del ministerio de enseñanza de Pablo que cien sermones podrían decirnos. Pablo enseñó a un joven tan bien porque Pablo primero había estudiado a ese joven.

blocks.en: The teacher must be willing to listen — to listen more than the teacher speaks, in some weeks. The teacher must be willing to learn from the student. The student often teaches the teacher something the teacher could not have learned any other way: what it is like to come to this passage of Scripture as a young person, or as a new convert, or as someone who has just lost a parent, or as someone who has just given his life to Christ. The teacher who refuses to learn from the student stops being a teacher very quickly. The teacher who learns from the student keeps growing as long as the class keeps meeting.
blocks.es_reference: El maestro debe estar dispuesto a escuchar — a escuchar más de lo que el maestro habla, en algunas semanas. El maestro debe estar dispuesto a aprender del estudiante. El estudiante a menudo le enseña al maestro algo que el maestro no podría haber aprendido de ninguna otra manera: cómo es venir a este pasaje de la Escritura como un joven, o como un nuevo convertido, o como alguien que acaba de perder a un padre, o como alguien que acaba de entregar su vida a Cristo. El maestro que rehúsa aprender del estudiante deja de ser maestro muy rápidamente. El maestro que aprende del estudiante sigue creciendo mientras la clase siga reuniéndose.

blocks.en: V. A Student of the Teaching Process
blocks.es_reference: V. Un estudiante del proceso de enseñanza

blocks.en: The teacher must also be a student of the teaching process itself. How is a lesson planned? How is the time prepared? How is the material presented? How is the lesson evaluated afterward? These are skills that must be learned and practiced.
blocks.es_reference: El maestro también debe ser un estudiante del proceso de enseñanza mismo. ¿Cómo se planifica una lección? ¿Cómo se prepara el tiempo? ¿Cómo se presenta el material? ¿Cómo se evalúa la lección después? Estas son habilidades que deben aprenderse y practicarse.

blocks.en: A person who knows the Bible and loves the students and walks with God can still fail in the classroom if he does not know how to teach. The next six units of this course are devoted to the craft of teaching — to the learning environment (U5), to lesson planning and aims (U6), to methods and strategies (U7), to questioning and case study and experiential study (U8), to Bible learning activities (U9), and to the children's sermon (U10). All of those exist because the teacher must take the teaching itself seriously as a discipline.
blocks.es_reference: Una persona que conoce la Biblia y ama a los estudiantes y anda con Dios todavía puede fracasar en el aula si no sabe cómo enseñar. Las siguientes seis unidades de este curso están dedicadas al oficio de enseñar — al ambiente de aprendizaje (U5), al plan de lección y a los objetivos (U6), a los métodos y estrategias (U7), a la pregunta, el estudio de caso y el estudio experiencial (U8), a las actividades de aprendizaje bíblico (U9), y al sermón para niños (U10). Todas existen porque el maestro debe tomar la enseñanza misma con seriedad como disciplina.

blocks.en: A pastor would not stand behind the pulpit on Sunday morning without preparation. A teacher should not stand in front of a class on Sunday morning without preparation either. The teaching ministry deserves the same care that the preaching ministry deserves. The Christian Education classroom is not a lesser room.
blocks.es_reference: Un pastor no se pararía detrás del púlpito el domingo por la mañana sin preparación. Un maestro tampoco debería pararse delante de una clase el domingo por la mañana sin preparación. El ministerio de enseñanza merece el mismo cuidado que merece el ministerio de predicación. El aula de Educación Cristiana no es un cuarto menor.

blocks.en: VI. A Person of Prayer
blocks.es_reference: VI. Una persona de oración

blocks.en: Finally, the teacher must be a person of prayer. The teacher must pray for himself — that the Spirit who breathed the Scripture would also breathe through the teaching of it. The teacher must pray for the students — by name, week by week, as a shepherd prays for sheep. The teacher must pray over the teaching-learning process itself — over the lesson, over the classroom, over the response.
blocks.es_reference: Finalmente, el maestro debe ser una persona de oración. El maestro debe orar por sí mismo — que el Espíritu que respiró la Escritura también respire a través de la enseñanza de ella. El maestro debe orar por los estudiantes — por nombre, semana tras semana, como un pastor ora por sus ovejas. El maestro debe orar sobre el proceso de enseñanza-aprendizaje mismo — sobre la lección, sobre el aula, sobre la respuesta.

blocks.en: The teacher who does not pray relies on himself. Reliance on oneself is the surest way to ruin a Bible class. The teacher who prays relies on the Spirit, and the Spirit is the One whose presence makes the Bible class different from a book club.
blocks.es_reference: El maestro que no ora se apoya en sí mismo. El apoyarse en uno mismo es la manera más segura de arruinar una clase bíblica. El maestro que ora se apoya en el Espíritu, y el Espíritu es Aquel cuya presencia hace que la clase bíblica sea diferente de un club de lectura.

blocks.en: A teacher's prayer for his students may sound something like this:
blocks.es_reference: La oración de un maestro por sus estudiantes puede sonar algo así:

blocks.en: "Lord, this Sunday I will stand before children whom you love. I cannot reach their hearts; I can only reach their ears. Reach their hearts. Use the words I will say. Forgive the words I will say wrongly. Give me sensitivity to know which student needs encouragement today and which student needs gentle correction. Give me patience with the one who is restless. Give me wisdom with the one who is asking honest questions. And after the class is over, follow each student home and continue what you began here."
blocks.es_reference: «Señor, este domingo me pararé ante niños a quienes tú amas. Yo no puedo alcanzar sus corazones; sólo puedo alcanzar sus oídos. Alcanza tú sus corazones. Usa las palabras que diré. Perdona las palabras que diré mal. Dame sensibilidad para saber cuál estudiante necesita ánimo hoy y cuál estudiante necesita corrección suave. Dame paciencia con el que está inquieto. Dame sabiduría con el que está haciendo preguntas honestas. Y después de que la clase termine, sigue a cada estudiante a casa y continúa lo que comenzaste aquí».

blocks.en: Such a prayer does not need to be elegant. It needs to be earnest, and it needs to be regular.
blocks.es_reference: Tal oración no necesita ser elegante. Necesita ser sincera, y necesita ser regular.

blocks.en: Closing: Six Things, None Optional
blocks.es_reference: Cierre: Seis cosas, ninguna opcional

blocks.en: Six characteristics of the Christian Education teacher: a person of God, a student of the Word, a servant, a student of the students, a student of the teaching process, a person of prayer. None of them can be safely omitted.
blocks.es_reference: Seis características del maestro de Educación Cristiana: una persona de Dios, un estudiante de la Palabra, un siervo, un estudiante de los estudiantes, un estudiante del proceso de enseñanza, una persona de oración. Ninguna de ellas puede ser omitida con seguridad.

blocks.en: The teacher who omits the first becomes a religious lecturer. The teacher who omits the second becomes an opinion-giver. The teacher who omits the third becomes a tyrant. The teacher who omits the fourth becomes irrelevant. The teacher who omits the fifth becomes ineffective. The teacher who omits the sixth becomes a self-reliant fool.
blocks.es_reference: El maestro que omite la primera se vuelve un conferencista religioso. El maestro que omite la segunda se vuelve un opinador. El maestro que omite la tercera se vuelve un tirano. El maestro que omite la cuarta se vuelve irrelevante. El maestro que omite la quinta se vuelve ineficaz. El maestro que omite la sexta se vuelve un necio que se apoya en sí mismo.

blocks.en: The teacher who keeps all six becomes what God uses to do His work in the heart of a learner. That is the calling of every reader of this book.
blocks.es_reference: El maestro que mantiene las seis se convierte en lo que Dios usa para hacer Su obra en el corazón de un aprendiz. Esa es la vocación de cada lector de este libro.

blocks.en: In Unit 3 we will look at the teacher whose example informs all six: Jesus, the Master Teacher.
blocks.es_reference: En la Unidad 3 veremos al maestro cuyo ejemplo informa las seis: Jesús, el Maestro de Maestros.

blocks.en: Unit 2 Examination
blocks.es_reference: Examen de la Unidad 2

blocks.en: Certificate of Ministry: 20 multiple-choice questions, 90% (18 of 20) to pass. Master of Theology & Master of Divinity: 20 MC + 10 short-answer, both at 90% independently. Each MC scores immediately when you click. MC must be passed before SA scores count. A failure locks the relevant section for 15 minutes; if you have already passed MC, only SA locks after an SA fail.
blocks.es_reference: Certificado de Ministerio: 20 preguntas de opción múltiple, 90% (18 de 20) para aprobar. Maestría en Teología y Maestría en Divinidad: 20 OM + 10 respuesta corta, ambas al 90% de forma independiente. Cada OM califica de inmediato al hacer clic. Debe aprobar OM antes de que cuente la sección RC. Una reprobación bloquea la sección por 15 minutos; si ya aprobó OM, solo se bloquea RC tras un fallo de RC.

mc.stem: What is the most important element in the teaching-learning process, according to Andi?
mc.why: Andi opens the unit with this thesis: the teacher outweighs curriculum, classroom, and textbook combined, because the student remembers the teacher's character long after the lesson is forgotten.

mc.stem: What is the anchor scripture for Unit 2?
mc.why: 2 Timothy 2:2 anchors this unit because it shows Paul describing the teacher in five attributes (faithful, having heard, tested by witnesses, able to teach, multiplying others) without mentioning curriculum or classroom.

mc.stem: In 2 Timothy 2:2, to whom does Paul tell Timothy to commit what he has heard?
options: Faithful men who shall be able to teach others also
mc.why: Paul deliberately broadens the teaching role beyond apostles or pastors. The teacher in his vision is any faithful person who can pass the truth on to another faithful person.

mc.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the six characteristics of the teacher named in Unit 2?
mc.why: The six are: person of God, student of the Word, servant, student of the students, student of the teaching process, person of prayer. Wealth is never named in the New Testament's profile of the teacher.

mc.stem: What does Andi say is the teacher's first work?
mc.why: In Section I Andi says the classroom does not begin Sunday morning; it begins Tuesday afternoon when the teacher opens the Bible alone and asks the Holy Spirit to teach him first.

mc.stem: What is the difference Andi names between knowledge of the Bible and skill in handling the Bible?
options: Knowledge is for adults; skill is for children
Knowledge of the contents and skill in handling the contents are different things; the teacher needs both
Knowledge is optional; skill is required
mc.why: Knowledge is what the Bible says; skill is how to find and apply it. A teacher with knowledge but no skill cannot answer a child's question; one with skill but no knowledge has nothing to apply.

mc.stem: What did Jesus say about being great in Matthew 20:26-27?
options: He must be your servant / minister
He must be the most learned
mc.why: Jesus inverted the cultural model of authority. In his kingdom, greatness is measured in service, not station. The teacher who serves carries his authority by kneeling beside his student.

mc.stem: What does Andi mean by being a 'student of the students'?
options: Knowing students' names, families, needs, interests, and backgrounds
Sitting next to students during class
mc.why: Andi names six things specifically: names, families, needs, interests, backgrounds, and the questions students bring. It is relational, not procedural.

mc.stem: Whom does Paul mention by name as having raised Timothy in faith (2 Timothy 1:5)?
options: His grandmother Lois and his mother Eunice
mc.why: Paul knew not only Timothy's faith but also where it had been planted. The phrase 'your grandmother Lois' shows that Paul had taken time to study his student's whole household.

mc.stem: What four steps in the teaching process does Andi name?
mc.why: In Section V Andi names the four-part teaching cycle: plan it, prepare it, present it, evaluate it. The remaining units of the course will unfold each step in detail.

mc.stem: Why must the teacher be a student of the teaching process, according to Andi?
options: Because teaching skills must be learned and practiced; loving God and the students is not enough by itself
mc.why: Andi's blunt point: a person can know God, love students, and walk faithfully, and still fail in the classroom for lack of teaching skill. The next six units exist precisely because skill must be deliberately learned.

mc.stem: The teacher who does not pray relies on _____, according to Andi.
mc.why: Andi calls self-reliance 'the surest way to ruin a Bible class.' Prayer is what keeps the teacher tethered to the Spirit, who is the One who makes the Bible class different from a book club.

mc.stem: What does Andi say happens to the teacher who omits 'a person of God' from the six characteristics?
mc.why: A teacher who is not first a person of God may still talk about God competently, but the talk is academic only. He becomes a religious lecturer rather than a witness.

mc.stem: What does Andi say happens to the teacher who omits 'a servant' from the six characteristics?
mc.why: Authority without service becomes tyranny. Andi notes that a teacher who lords over students teaches them only resistance.

mc.stem: What does Andi say happens to the teacher who omits 'a student of the students' from the six characteristics?
mc.why: A teacher who never studies his students answers questions they are not asking and ignores the questions they are. The result is irrelevance.

mc.stem: What does Andi say happens to the teacher who omits 'a person of prayer' from the six characteristics?
mc.why: Without prayer, a teacher may know the Bible, love the students, and possess every skill — and still rely on himself. Andi calls this 'a self-reliant fool.'

mc.stem: What does Unit 3 cover, according to the Closing of Unit 2?
mc.why: All six characteristics in Unit 2 find their perfect example in Jesus, so Unit 3 turns the lens on him as the master teacher.

mc.stem: How does Andi describe the teacher's authority in the New Testament, in contrast to our culture?
options: A person of authority who stands above the student
A person without any real authority
A person of authority who serves the student
A person who has no opinions of his own
mc.why: Both elements are kept: real authority AND real service. The New Testament teacher is not stripped of authority, nor does he wield it from above. He stands beside the student in service.

mc.stem: In Section II, what does Andi say the Word should be to the teacher?
options: A reference book pulled from the shelf on Saturday night
A tool used only when there is a question to answer
A subject for academic study only
The teacher's daily food and constant companion
mc.why: The Word is not a Saturday-night reference book. Andi calls it the teacher's daily food and constant companion.

mc.stem: According to the orientation, what is the spirit in which Paul describes the teacher in 2 Timothy 2:2?
options: As one who lectures from authority alone
As a person above the student in every way
As a faithful person who has heard and can hand the truth on to another faithful person
mc.why: Paul's vision is hand-to-hand transmission: faithful person to faithful person to faithful person. No mention of curriculum, classroom, or hierarchy.
